newsitem.title: UK: UK worried at reports of pension firms' tactics.
newsitem.headline: UK worried at reports of pension firms' tactics.

text.p: The Treasury minister charged with pressing insurance companies which mis-sold pensions to pay compensation said on Friday she had reports that some firms were putting "unacceptable pressure" on people to settle.

Helen Liddell earlier this month published a "league table" of the major companies involved in the four billion stg mis-selling scandal showing the number of cases they had outstanding and the number they had settled.

She told parliament: "I am worried about reports I have that some individuals are being put under unacceptable pressure to settle deals they are being offered by companies who mis-sold them pensions as a means of reducing their statistics."
"I am not prepared to be hoodwinked by actions such as that, and I know that the responsible companies will be appalled to think that it is going on," she added.
Liddell, speaking in a short debate on the issue, said she would decide in the autumn what further steps she would take to put pressure on the companies.
"I will take account of the powers I already have. And, if new powers are required, I will not hesitate to seek a means of acquiring those new powers," she said.

As many as 1.5 million people may have been wrongly advised by the financial services industry to take out personal pensions in the late 1980s and early 1990s instead of staying in occupational schemes.
